bull_bear.body: Dividend recommended: ₹2/share FY26; capex prioritized over buybacks; no M&A mentioned; focus on organic growth and operational efficiency
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Aluminum price volatility (pass-through lag), labor cost escalation across states, geopolitical supply chain disruptions, delayed global program ramp-ups (e.g., JLR), margin compression from input inflation
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; CEO Sumit Bhatnagar emphasized 'Refocus, Reset, Rebuild' with disciplined execution; acknowledged past global missteps but confident in domestic rebound and new capacity; tone pragmatic, not overly bullish
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Over 50% power from renewables; employees arranged cooking fuel during gas shortages; cybersecurity capex flagged as strategic; ₹26cr one-off expenses include wage code + write-offs; JLR program now live after 18-month delay
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body: - Ongoing program to reduce interest cost/finance costs alongside continued reinvestment into capacity expansion (new Shikrapur facility) to support future growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Domestic: 80% of revenue; PV: strong SUV/hybrid demand; CV: +19.5% YoY volume growth; 2W: material contribution increase in Q4; Export: softness due to geopolitical headwinds; New: first non-auto win in data center turbo core compressor
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Pioneer in India for Low Pressure Die Casting (LPDC) and Gravity Die Casting (GDC); operates one of the largest aluminum foundries in India.
- Leader in the development of Pro-Cast and Magma space in India, with a diversified, marquee customer base and no reliance on a single anchor customer.
- 56-year track record, further enriched by the 89-year legacy of European subsidiary Illichmann Castalloy; group blends European engineering, Japanese quality (via Enkei) and Indian frugal engineering across 235+ cumulative years of experience.
- 4 modern manufacturing plants (3 in India - Pune x2, Binola; 1 international - Slovakia) plus an international marketing office in Austria, enabling a 'close-to-demand' global footprint for shorter time-to-market and cost optimisation.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body: - [Leadership] CEO Sumit Bhatnagar highlighted the new Shikrapur-area facility as a strategic step to support future growth, alongside continued focus on customer partnerships, manufacturing capabilities and building a scalable organisation.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin down 248bps YoY due to aluminum price pass-through lag (₹30-35cr Q4 impact), labor cost hike of 35% at Binola plant (Haryana wage code), energy/freight inflation; EBITDA margin pressured by mix shift to domestic/2W and one-off ₹26cr FY26 expenses
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 8-10% FY27 (excl. aluminum volatility); margin: expecting 1.5%+ EBITDA margin expansion; order inflow: new wins in EV axle (Germany), data center turbo core, premium 2W; capex/commissioning: ₹130-150cr FY27 for new plant, automation, machining, cybersecurity
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: ₹7,600 crore executable order book (FY26-FY31), excludes pre-FY26 revenue programs; includes new wins: German e-Axle housing, data center turbo core, premium Indian 2W part; rationalized 4 non-performing global/Indian programs
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: New manufacturing plant (1+ by FY27), entry into data center components, deeper penetration in Indian OEMs previously untapped, European EV/ICE program ramp-up, potential forward integration
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Alicon delivered record Q4 revenue driven by domestic automotive recovery and new non-auto wins, but margins were pressured by aluminum price lags and one-off labor cost hikes; the company is now resetting strategy with capacity expansion, automation, and renewed focus on India to unlock long-term growth from a ₹7,600 crore order book.
